ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.58 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method; send the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route-compliance record (RD-7); add flag_account for the second upheld route deviation within 90 days (RD-6).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat (F7), the written driver statement (F9) and the rider complaint contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; weather was fair (F14). No safety escalation.

Route deviation. Actual 13.1 km vs optimal 8.3 km = +4.8 km (F1), well over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The code isolates one off-route segment 09:07–09:14, 5.77 km driven where the optimal covers 1.10 km, adding 4.67 km (F3).

Notice/consent (RD-5): the driver's chat message at 09:03 — the pickup minute, before the 09:07 deviation — notified a traffic reason and proposed going via Marina Boulevard, so the notice is timely and the reason is genuine: New Bridge Road was in speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:54–09:14 (F10), i.e. heavy congestion, band 1–2 (RD-4). But notice alone is not consent. The rider never replied (F8: a single message, all timestamped), and a driver's later statement that the rider did not object is a claim, not consent; a driver's silence-based inference does not satisfy "the rider acknowledged" (RD-5). The rider's own complaint confirms she did not reply and he went anyway. No rider message covers the segment, so the segment is not exempt under RD-3 or RD-5.

Traffic reason with notice and no agreement falls in the RD-2 row "traffic reason, rider not informed/not agreed" → refund the excess distance fare (C3: same amount as no-traffic). Because the rider did not agree, the whole 4.67 km of the off-route segment is non-exempt.

Arithmetic: refundable km = 4.67; this trip's per-km distance fare = $1.4097/km (F4). 4.67 × 1.4097 = $6.5833 ≈ $6.58. The billed excess of $6.77 (F4) corresponds to the full 4.80 km actual-minus-optimal; only the segment km at the trip's own rate are refunded, so the amount is $6.58. Surge was 1.0× (F5) and tolls/time fare are not refunded, so nothing else is added.

Account: this is an upheld deviation against the driver, and his profile shows 2 upheld route deviations in 90 days (F16), so RD-6 applies — flag_account add-on. As a notification-related incident, RD-7's reminder and log apply (no formal warning for a first such incident). Per TH-1/TH-2 the amount is under $10, so the system rules finally (C1/DISP-001).

Precedents: DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute, refund of excess distance fare) is the closest precedent; the amount here is larger because the deviation is larger.

segment_findings.reason: Driver notified at 09:03, before the 09:07 segment began, citing New Bridge Road congestion, which F10 confirms (band 2, 08:54–09:14) — so the traffic reason under RD-4 is established. But the rider never replied (F8 shows one message only, timestamped; the driver's post-trip statement F9 that she 'did not object' is a claim, not evidence of acknowledgment). Notice without agreement = RD-5 not satisfied and RD-3 not engaged, so the segment is not exempt; under RD-2 (traffic reason, rider not informed/agreed → refund excess distance fare) the segment 'counts' and its 4.67 km are refundable at the trip's $1.4097/km.

element_findings.element: RD-5 notice: timely in-app chat notice before/at the point of deviation, with a reason
element_findings.reason: Chat #1 at 09:03 (pickup time, before the 09:07 segment) is an in-app message from the driver and it gives a brief reason (New Bridge Road traffic). Message is timestamped (F8), and the cited congestion is corroborated by the traffic feed (F10).

element_findings.element: RD-5 consent: rider acknowledged the reroute
element_findings.reason: The chat record contains only the driver's one message; there is no rider reply or call acknowledgment. The driver's written statement that the rider did not object is a claim, not consent (RD-5). Rider's complaint confirms she did not reply.
The only named road (Marina Boulevard) was named by the driver, not requested by the rider, and was not accepted by her before the segment began.
Driver profile shows 2 upheld route deviations in the last 90 days; this case is an upheld deviation, so the flag_account add-on applies (profile used only for the add-on, not to decide the case).
Multiplier was 1.0× — no surge, so no surge notice/differential arises; no surge refund.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that the rider raised no objection is a claim about verbal assent with no chat or call-recording support; a rider's silence in response to a reroute proposal is not acknowledgment under RD-5.
Sentosa Gateway band 4 and Kampong Bahru Road band 5 show no congestion; they do not support the reroute and are not on the displaced part of the optimal route.
The driver's prior upheld route deviations are used only for the RD-6 flag add-on; a profile fact never decides the current case.
